html:
A small brick chapel in Ravenna, built between about 425 and 450, with some of the best preserved early Christian mosaics anywhere. It is shaped like a cross and was first attached to a larger church, now gone.

From outside it is plain. Inside, every upper surface is covered in mosaic. The central vault is deep blue, scattered with hundreds of gold stars around a cross. Over one door Christ appears as the Good Shepherd among his sheep; over another, Saint Lawrence walks toward the gridiron on which he was martyred. Deer drink from a spring, a symbol of souls thirsting for God. Thin panes of alabaster let in a soft light.

The name links it to the empress Galla Placidia, who ruled from Ravenna, but she died and was buried in Rome. Since 1996 it has been a World Heritage Site together with seven other early Christian buildings in Ravenna, among them San Vitale.
